rows.description: A friend says "I will not share with you, you are not my friend". It stings. I can say "that makes me sad" and go play elsewhere. I should not be blamed for wanting a share, and a teacher can help us take turns.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, envy, fairness, generosity
related mind states: sadness

rows.description: The teacher says my name sternly in front of the class. My face burns and I want to hide. Wise help is a quiet talk after and a chance to fix it. A harsh public telling-off can make a child feel bad instead of learning what to do.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear, gratitude, humiliation, resentment, respect, trust
related mind states: shame

rows.description: The teacher shows me gently how to hold the pencil again and smiles. I feel helped, not judged. I learn that being corrected is part of learning and does not mean I am bad, and I try again with pride.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear, humiliation, resentment, respect, shame, trust
related mind states: gratitude, pride

rows.description: I was scolded for something my friend also did. I feel it is unfair and I go quiet and cross. A wise adult listens to my side. The immature pattern is sulking, being rude to the teacher or blaming a friend to escape.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear, gratitude, humiliation, respect, shame, trust
related mind states: resentment

rows.description: I know my teacher corrects me because she cares whether I am safe and learning. I feel able to say "sorry, I will do better". A trusting child can hear a correction and still feel loved.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear, gratitude, humiliation, resentment, respect, shame
related mind states: affection, trust

rows.description: A teacher laughs at my mistake or calls me lazy or silly in front of everyone. I feel small and afraid of school. This is not my fault; telling a parent helps. Children need correction without ridicule.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: fear, gratitude, resentment, respect, shame, trust
related mind states: amusement, playfulness, fear, humiliation

rows.description: My teacher says "well done, you tried so hard" and gives me a star. I feel tall and happy. Praise for effort makes me want to keep trying, while praise only for being the best can make me fear mistakes.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, affection, envy
related mind states: joy, fear, pride

rows.description: My parent hugs me and says "I am proud of you" after I tie my shoes. I feel safe and loved and eager to show more. I learn I am loved for who I am, not only for what I do.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, envy, pride
related mind states: affection, excitement, pride, trust

rows.description: After the teacher praises me, a classmate frowns and says "you are not that good". I feel confused and a little sad. A wise response is to stay kind and not brag; the classmate's feeling is envy, not proof I did wrong.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, affection, pride
related mind states: sadness, confusion, envy

rows.description: Dadi claps when I recite a poem and tells everyone. I glow but also feel shy. Family pride is warm and I enjoy it. Too much showing-off pressure can make a child perform for approval instead of for joy.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: admiration, affection, envy
related mind states: joy, shyness, pride
